newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates steady, big bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates steady, big bank lending.

text.p: Interbank rates were little changed on Wednesday with Bank Negara Malaysia seen providing more liquidity to the market, dealers said.
"A big bank is lending one-month money at 8.5 percent, said to be on behalf of Bank Negara," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "There has not been much movements. The market is still quite tight."
There was no confirmation of the funds injection from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market operations.
One-, two- and three-week money were all unchanged at 8.50/70 percent.
One-month money was steady at 8.50 percent and three-month at 8.00/30 percent.
The overnight was expected to continue trading between 8.30 and 8.80 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said despite injection of fresh funds by the central bank, the market remained short, partially caused by month-end ringgit demand.
But rates may come off slightly at the end of the week due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit, they said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were also steady.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.27, or an implied yield of 7.73 percent.
The December contract was unchanged at 92.50, or 7.50 percent.
